teaser.en: Called the 'crown of honour', this bush legume is used in charms meant to raise a person above their rivals.

summary.en: *Chitadzi* is a dry-country shrub with feathery leaves and large mauve pea flowers. It is used in medicine, for walking sticks and light building, and in magic to crown a person to dominance.

about.en: *Chitadzi* is a shrub with leaves made of many small, paired leaflets, giving it a fine, feathery look. Its flowers are large for the plant, mauve pea-flowers that stand out against the grey-green bush.

where.en: It grows in dry lowlands and coastal bushland.

uses.en: Roots, leaves and even the ash of the plant are used in traditional medicine. Its straight stems are used in light construction and made into walking sticks.

culture.en: Its name is explained as 'crown of honour'. It is used magically to crown someone to dominance: a charm for rank and respect.

names.en: Pakia records *chitadzi*; ICRAF's handbook gives *mkitaji*, which is also the Swahili name. In Giriama it is *mkitaji* or *kitwadzi*. There is no common English name; botanists call it *Ormocarpum kirkii*.

reason.en: Another bush plant used as a social charm
Sicklebush, a legume of the same bushland
Winter cassia, a bush legume used in medicine
